answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote on work, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraudulent claims. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply influence for free: each account needs its own stake, and colluding accounts risk losing it together. The ivory ledger can track those losses, while saffron-tagged audits make suspicious clusters easier to review; attackers must continually fund identities that may wander into costly scrutiny.
